newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end high after crossing 600 mark.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end high after crossing 600 mark.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed up on Monday as retailers began buying, hoping to cash in on good new year prospects, brokers said.

The Colombo Stock Exchange all-share index closed 3.4 points higher at 602.6, crossing the psychological 600-point barrier for the first time in three weeks. The all-share index fell below the barrier on December 6.
"When it breaks, chances are there for prices to pick up further in the short run," a broker for Bartleet Mallory said.
"Today's activity was centred around retailers who were collecting quantity hoping prices will climb in January."
Turnover, supported by 249,900 blue-chip conglomerate Hayleys at 180 rupees a share, and 150,000 Sampath Bank at 46 rupees per share, was a healthy 58.8 million rupees.
More than 200,000 Ceylon Grain Elevators also traded hands at prices between 13.75 and 14.50 per share. Gains outnumbered losses 20 to eight. Foreign purchases were 1.6 million rupees.

"We didn't actually expect it to climb back up so soon," said Rajiv Casie Chitty, manager research at CT Smith Stockbrokers. "It clearly shows there is strong support for the market at the 600 level," he said.
